full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the order dated 12.02.2013 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal; 1 Dhaka in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 01 of 2012 dismissing the appeal. 

 2. Facts of the case, in brief, are that Md. Salek Uddin, respondent herein filed A.T. Case No. 10 of 1996 before the Administrative Tribunal, Bogra, which was allowed on 06.7.1998 in favour of the respondent. The Tribunal below declared the dismissal order of the respondent as illegal and directed the petitioners to reinstate him and to allow him to go on compulsory retirement from the date of retirement   and to give him pension benefits. 

 4. Thereafter, the respondent filed Miscellaneous A.T. Case No. 8 of 2008 (Execution Case) before the Administrative Tribunal, Bogra, for Executing the order dated 06.07.1998 passed in A.T. Case No. 10 of 1998. After hearing the parties the said miscellaneous case was allowed by order dated 17.01.2012. 

 5. Against the aforesaid order dated 17.01.2012, the petitioners filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 01 of 2012 before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka. Upon hearing the parties concerned the miscellaneous appeal was dismissed upholding the order passed by the Administrative Tribunal, Borga in Miscellaneous A.T. Case No. 08 of 2008. 

 6. Mr. Md. Hefzul Bari, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the application made by the respondent in Miscellaneous A. T. Case No. 08 of 2008 (Execution) was not maintainable under section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980 and it is barred by limitation. He further submits that the respondent had already availed service benefits without raising any objection and all his due pension benefits had already been paid and as such, the Administrative Tribunal as well as the Administrative Appellate Tribunal erred in passing the impugned orders. 

 9. It appears that the. Administrative Tribunal in A.T. Case No. 10 of 1996 passed an order directing the concerned authority to reinstate the respondent and from the date of reinstatement to allow him to go on compulsory retirement giving all the due benefits. The order of the Administrative Tribunal dated 06.07.1998, was upheld by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal in A.A.T Appeal No. 78 of 1998 where the appeal preferred by the Government of Bangladesh represented by the Agrani Bank Limited, was dismissed by judgment and order dated 05.11.2007. 

 10. However, since the Agrani Bank was not complying with the order of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, the respondent filed Miscellaneous A.T. Case No. 8 of 2008 (Execution) under order  XXI Rule 37 and 38 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Upon hearing the parties the application was allowed by order dated 17.01.2012 directing the concerned authorities to pay all the dues to the respondent up to 26.10.2008, the date on which he was reinstated. This order was upheld by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal by the impugned judgment dated 12.02.2013.
